text: The earth could not bear two suns, nor Asia two kings.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Alexander
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: I take this for a wise man, who chose rather to commit himself to a good man than to a strong place.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Alexander
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: Enough for you to receive, but not for me to give.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Alexander
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: I had rather be called merciful a great while, than lord a little while.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Philip
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: Whether we will be well or ill spoken of is in our own power.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Philip
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: Only honorable things are honorable, and only just things are just.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Antigonus
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: It is better for him to die than to live, who must be weary not only of his enemies, but of his friends too.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Dion
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878

text: Those I made first, but now I make these by my valor and industry.
source: Plutarch, Apophthegms of Kings and Great Commanders: Agathocles
translator: Several hands, ed. W. W. Goodwin, 1878
